explanation: Copper oxide dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid to form blue-green copper(II) chloride solution — NCERT's example showing that metal oxides react with acids the same way bases do, which is why they're called basic oxides.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Black copper oxide powder in colourless dilute hydrochloric acid.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A blue-green copper chloride solution, the powder dissolved.
beaker_view.observation: The black powder dissolves into the acid, turning the solution a distinct blue-green.
